To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hierarchical three-dimensional ( 3D) branchoed hematite nanorods arrays (NAs), which exhibited high photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting performance, were prepared by a facile two-step electrodeposition approach.

the hierarchical three-dimensional branched nanorods arrays of hematite on FTO substrates exhibit enhanced photoelectrochemical activity for water splitting due to enhanced visible light absorption and charge separation.

hierarchical 3D branches hematite NAs were successfully fabricated on FTO substrates, and exhibited high PEC performance due to the enhanced light absorption, charge separation and transfer, and the introduction of a Ti0 2 underlayer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a facile and low-cost strategy for the synthesis of hierarchical 3D brancho hematite NAs on FTO glass substrates, and the as-prepared branched hematite arrays exhibit high PEC water-splitting performance.
the design of 3D branced hematite NAs, which is a simple, low-cost and effective strategy for the fabrication of high-efficiency photoanodes for photoelectrochemical solar water splitting.
a facile, low-cost, and scalable method to fabricate high-efficiency photoanodes with a hierarchical 3D branached structure for PEC water splitting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the introduction of a Ti0.8Nb0.2O2 underlayer and the hierarchical 3D branchoed hematite NAs on FTO conductive glass substrats are promising for the development of high-efficiency photoanodes for PEC water splitting.

the hierarchical 3D branached hematite NAs with a TiO2 layer on FTO conductive glass substratesshowed a promising PEC water splitting property with a low onset potential, high photocurrent density and long-term stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully fabricated a 3D branced hematite NAs photoanode with enhanced mid-visible-light absorption, which can be a promising candidate for high-efficiency PEC water splitting.
the 3D branced hematite NAs can be regarded as a new type of photoanode for efficient PEC water splitting.
the introduction of TiO2 underlayers and the formation of 3D branches can significantly improve the PEC performance of the hematite-based photoanodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3D branches of hematite NAs could provide a large surface area and more active sites for photoelectrocatalysis, and thus improve the photoconversion efficiency of the hematite photoanode for water splitting.
the hierarchical 3D branached hematite NAs with enhanced mid-visible absorption can be an ideal PEC photoanode material with great potential in practical applications.
hierarchical 3D branced hematite NAs on FTO conductive glass can be used as high-efficiency photoanodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting.
